topic: A sidereal day on Venus (243 Earth days) is longer than its year (225 Earth days); the solar day is ~117 Earth days

fact_check.claim: Venus rotates once every ~243 Earth days (retrograde) and orbits the Sun in ~224.7 Earth days; its solar day (noon to noon) is ~116.75 Earth days.
fact_check.source_hint: NASA Venus fact sheet / NASA Planetary Fact Sheet. Keep 'day' definitions explicit to avoid the common misleading headline.

hooks: A day on Venus is longer than its year.
Venus finishes a year before it finishes one spin.
It spins backwards. And sunrise takes 117 days.
titles: A Day On Venus Is Longer Than Its Year (Here's The Catch)
243 Days To Spin, 225 Days To Orbit — The Planet That Breaks Clocks
Why Venus Has Three Different 'Days' And None Agree

beats.vo: A day on Venus is longer than its year.
beats.visual: Venus fills frame, already rotating; giant '243' slams on screen on frame 1

beats.vo: Venus needs 243 Earth days to spin once. It circles the Sun in only 225.
beats.visual: Two counters side by side racing at different speeds

beats.vo: So the planet finishes a whole year before it finishes one rotation. Everywhere else in the solar system, days are the short part.
beats.visual: Solar system strip with fast little planets, Venus frozen almost still

beats.vo: It also spins backwards. On Venus, the Sun rises in the west.
beats.visual: Rotation arrow flips direction; sunrise wipes right-to-left

beats.vo: And here's the part that breaks the headline: sunrise to sunrise is just 117 days.
beats.visual: Big '117' punches in; music drops for one beat

beats.vo: Because 'day' has two meanings. One full spin takes 243 days. But the planet is also moving around the Sun, so noon returns every 117 days.
beats.visual: Top-down orbit diagram with a marker for noon, showing the two clocks

beats.vo: Same planet, three clocks, none of them matching. That's the whole trick.
beats.visual: Three counters stack into one frame; cut back to the opening Venus shot
Final frame identical to frame 1 for the loop

payoff: The headline is true only for a sidereal day; 'day' has more than one definition.
cta: Which number should count as a day: 243 or 117?
pinned_comment: 243 (one spin) or 117 (sunrise to sunrise) — which one gets to be called a 'day'? Drop a number 👇
description:
A day on Venus is longer than its year — but only if you mean one full spin.

Venus rotates once every ~243 Earth days, orbits the Sun in ~225, and spins backwards. Because it's also moving along its orbit, noon-to-noon takes ~117 Earth days. Three clocks, one planet.

Which number should count as a day: 243 or 117?

Figures: NASA Planetary Fact Sheet. Educational summary.
